lead: Machinery and equipment for farms, smallholdings, woodlands and apiaries, from compact and vintage tractors to implements, harvest, livestock, forestry and beekeeping gear, organised by job; production machines stay at kind level, while vintage tractors, stationary engines and beehives are mapped to named archetypes.

depts.note: Current tractors at kind level; sizes from sub-compact to articulated. Vintage tractors have their own department.

b.m: Power and fit to the job
b.w: Measured PTO and drawbar power against the job, plus hitch category and which implements fit; fit to the job comes first.
Measured in the Nebraska (OECD) tractor test.
Owner surveys put dealer support first.

b.v: gear / shuttle < powershift < hydrostatic or CVT (for convenience)
b.w: Hydrostatic dominates sub-compact and compact; CVT at the top of farm ranges.
Cab, air conditioning and sound level are compared in tests.
Matched to the work, not a ladder.

s.brief: Tier shelf for smallholders and acreage owners. Sub-compact (under ~25 hp, mid-mount mower), compact (~25–60 hp) and utility (~60–120 hp) tractors as separate kinds; two-wheel (walk-behind) tractors and power tillers. Name the market-covering makers per kind (e.g. Kubota, John Deere, Mahindra, LS, Kioti, New Holland, Massey Ferguson, Yanmar, Iseki, TYM; two-wheel: BCS, Grillo, Pasquali, Honda, Kubota) and any independent test/review winner; add model ranges (r) rather than SKUs. Note Japanese grey-import compacts as a type. Strip the single production model from old k1 and re-source.

New kind; split out of the old utility tractor aliases.

New kind; walk-behind tractor with PTO for implements (BCS, Grillo, Pasquali); power tiller as alias/type.

depts.note: Collector department: kind → archetype (model family) → version (series, fuel, generation) → detail, following the TractorData maker → model axis.

s.brief: Variety shelf; ordered by significance, archetypes are model families with versions. Required icons: Fordson Model F and N, Ferguson TE20 (TEA/TED/TEF versions) and Ford 9N/2N/8N, Farmall Regular/F-20/H/M, John Deere two-cylinder (Model D, A, B, 'Johnny Popper'), Lanz Bulldog (hot-bulb). Also: Waterloo Boy, IH Titan/Mogul, Hart-Parr, Allis-Chalmers WC, Massey-Harris, Massey Ferguson 35/135, David Brown Cropmaster, Field Marshall, Fordson Major, Fendt Dieselross, Deutz F-series, Porsche-Diesel, Hanomag, Zetor, Ursus C-45, Landini Velite, SAME, Steiger. Steam: Burrell, Fowler ploughing engines, Case. Crawlers: Holt, Caterpillar Twenty/Sixty/D2, Cletrac. Use TractorData and Wikipedia; add brand-register entries for heritage makers. Cross-link scale models to Toys, not here.

s.brief: Variety shelf for the stationary-engine hobby and rally machinery. Archetypes: hit-and-miss (Fairbanks-Morse Z, IHC Famous/Mogul, Hercules, Associated, Stover, Galloway), throttle-governed (Lister D and CS, Petter, Wolseley WD, Ruston Hornsby), hot-bulb (Bolinder, Ruston, Blackstone), plus threshing machines (Ransomes, Marshall, Clayton & Shuttleworth) and horse-drawn implements. Source via Wikipedia and engine-collector references.
